_about: The Magic Portals port's portal shot. The owner said on 11 September that a tap fires a
shot from the character toward the tap, and the portal opens where it arrives. A wall, a
crate or a stone on the way stops it, and a shot that fails costs nothing. The Godot project
opens a portal at the tap at once, so this is the port's. See
docs/planning/2026-09-11-magic-portals-remaster.md, step 8; the flight's numbers are the

_source: ETHCallback_projectile (Portal.angelscript, bytes 358053..359141), the projectile.ent the global
addProjectile (354113..355121) adds, listing out/parity/asbc/all_functions.txt (md5
48fe65ce8baea16b94ed84d8d7be84b0) L71109, arguments pushed last-first. The callback runs ONCE a
frame, and its first run falls straight through into the common block, so the first frame does
both:
#1-12    CheckCustomData('initialPos'): absent on the first run
#14-27   SetVector2('initialPos', GetPositionXY()): where it was spawned, BEFORE the jump
#29-55   AddToPositionXY(direction x g_scale.scale(24)): the first-frame jump of 24 units
#57-71   AddScaledEntity('projectile_shoot.ent', GetPosition()): the flash, AFTER the jump
#74-125  every run: angle = degrees(getAngle(dir)) - 90, then
AddToPositionXY(dir x g_timeManager.scaledUnitsPerSecond(200)): the advance
#127-156 squaredDistance(initialPos, GetPositionXY()) > GetFloat('squaredDistance') (CMPf, JNP: a
STRICT greater), the stored squaredDistance(finalPos, casterPos) addProjectile #94-110 wrote
#158-199 arrived: with 'willDie' clear insertPortal(destiny, preferedTeleportEntity); #201-263 else
the fail effects and playPortalFailedSound; #264-272 DeleteEntity(thisEntity)
So the shot is not snapped to its destination: it is carried past it by the last advance, the
portal opens at the stored `destiny` (the tap, here), and it arrives on the first frame k with
24 + k x (200 x ms / 1000) > the distance - the jump is part of the first frame's travel.
The advance's clock: STimeManager::scaledUnitsPerSecond (bytes 8284..8363) = unitsPerSecond x
g_scale.getScale(), and unitsPerSecond (8045..8162 ins 3-15) = speed x min(200,
GetLastFrameElapsedTime()) / 1000 x m_factor - the script's FLOORED whole milliseconds (clock.json,
planning step 147), 16 at the 60 Hz the program matches: 200 x 16 / 1000 = 3.2 units a frame, 192 a
second of wall time, not 200 and not the guess of 600 this file held until step 149. In the
port's units g_scale.getScale() is 1 (motions.json says why). frame_cap_ms is that min's 200, the
same one motions.json's linear_motion carries.
WHEN IT FIRST RUNS (reference/ethanon/toolkit/Source/src/engine/Scene/). ETHScene::Update
(ETHScene.cpp:459-493) runs the physics (:464), then every ALWAYS-ACTIVE entity's callback
(ETHActiveEntityHandler.cpp:113-143 UpdateAlwaysActiveEntities; :70-73 says which: a callback and
not static - the projectile), then the script's scene update (:473-474; `loop`, main.angelscript
bytes 312880..313283, which LoadScene is given as the update function: PortalManager::update and
the tap), then the STATIC entities' callbacks (:488, ETHActiveEntityHandler.cpp:145-165: an
anti_portal_agent, a fire_agent, a reflect_agent). A tap's AddEntity (ETHScene.cpp:261-292) puts the
projectile in its bucket at once and on the dynamic list (ETHActiveEntityHandler.cpp:56-64), but
this frame's dynamic pass is over: its first callback runs on the NEXT frame, and a static agent
sees it at its spawn point on the frame it is fired. DeleteEntity erases it from its bucket at once
(ETHScene.cpp:924-927, ETHBucketManager.cpp:434-476), so a shot that arrives is gone before any
static callback of that frame looks.
The two facts that order rests on were read, not assumed. The flags: reference/extracted/assets/entities/
projectile.ent is static=0 with a callback (so always active), and anti_portal_agent.ent, fire_agent.ent,
reflect_agent.ent and anti_projectile_wall.ent are static=1. The tap: PortalManager::update is a GameController,
run by GameControllerManager::update (listing ins 6-24, CALLINTF GameController::update) from BaseState::loop (bytes
11245..11317 ins 6-8) under Game::loop (114414..114716), which the global `loop` reaches through
SStateManager::runCurrentLoopFunction (9012..9068): inside the scene-update function, never inside an entity's
callback, so the dynamic pass of the tap's frame is already over when it adds the projectile.
In the port's tick the order is the same cycle cut elsewhere: Game::AfterStep (the shot's callback
and the static ones, Portals::Tick) runs BEFORE readInput (the tap) in MagicPortalsLayer::fixedTick, so
the first Tick after Shoot is already the next frame's and no delay is added; the static pass of the
tap's own frame, between the two, is the first pass of that Tick (Portals::Flight::fresh).

_note: What a reflect_agent does to a shot. The owner said on 11 September that it reflects
the shot 'under an angle', and did not know how far it goes on; they will judge that by
playing. So the shot comes off mirrored across the reflector's plane and goes on for the
rest of the distance it was fired: a flat reflector sends it to the tap mirrored across
it. reflect_agent.ent has no collision (shape 0) and no size, so how near a shot has to
pass is not the original's either: half its 32 px sprite. The original's script keeps
a hasBeenReflected flag, not a count, so a shot comes off one reflector at most.
(G9 builds the original's 32 and its leg; step 149 leaves both as they were.)
_default_plane: The plane of a reflector whose level gives none. One placement in the game does:
level26a's reflect_agent_ent_961. reflect_agent.ent carries no default, and the Godot project
reads a missing plane as vertical (behaviours.gd:246), so the port does too.
